metadata.name: stage4-routeros-pathb-deployment
metadata.description: Render and optionally apply the RouterOS CHR Path B lab configuration for the isolated 10.9.8.0/24 iPXE segment.

variables.name: ansible_root
variables.description: Ansible subtree containing the RouterOS Path B playbook and role.

variables.name: inventory
variables.description: Inventory containing the routeros_pathb host group and install_targets metadata.

variables.name: limit_target
variables.description: RouterOS host entry to render or apply.

variables.name: render_root
variables.description: Local filesystem location where the role renders the .rsc file and JSON manifest.

variables.name: apply_changes
variables.description: Set to true to upload and import the generated .rsc script over SSH.

stages.summary: Validate the RouterOS Path B playbook syntax before touching the RouterOS host.
Render the RouterOS .rsc configuration and machine-readable JSON manifest locally without applying them.
Review architecture and service constraints before attempting a live apply.
command: printf 'Review rendered manifest for x86 CHR constraints: ZeroTier unsupported on x86, RouterOS native syslog receive unavailable, HTTP disabled rather than redirected.\n'

stages.summary: Upload and import the generated RouterOS configuration. Use only when SSH access, package payloads, and rollback path are ready.
notes: If apply_changes=false, this stage is a no-op render validation.
RouterOS package uploads require package payloads to be present locally and may require reboot to take effect.
Container support on RouterOS requires physical-access-style enablement per MikroTik guidance.

stages.summary: Validate serial, SSH, DHCP, iPXE handoff, and management-plane services after the RouterOS config is active.
command: printf 'Validate: serial console, SSH, DHCP next-server/boot-file, HTTPS, NTP, SNMP, and remote syslog client behavior.\n'
